fields.before: The correct answer is イ (10.5 hours). The earliest time at which all the tasks finish can be found by adding up the earliest finish time of each task from the beginning. There are only two steps: (1) if a task has a single predecessor, add its own task time to that predecessor finish time; (2) if a task has several predecessors, first line up with the one that finishes latest, and then add. Working it out: ① finishes at 0.5 hours. ② takes 2 hours after ①, so it finishes at 2.5 hours, and ③ takes 1 hour after ①, so it finishes at 1.5 hours. ④ can start only after both ② and ③ are done, so it starts from the later of the two, 2.5 hours, takes 3 hours, and finishes at 5.5 hours. After ④, tasks ⑤, ⑥ and ⑦ can all start at the same time, so ⑤ finishes at 7.5 hours, ⑥ at 8.5 hours, and ⑦ at 7.0 hours. The last task ⑧ waits until all three are done, so it starts from the latest one, ⑥ at 8.5 hours, takes 2 hours, and finishes at 10.5 hours. The earliest overall finish time is therefore 10.5 hours. This matches the total of the longest path ①→②→④→⑥→⑧ (0.5+2+3+3+2).

fields.before: The correct answer is エ, the consolidated balance sheet. A balance sheet (B/S) is a financial statement that shows, at one point in time — the closing date — how much property a company holds (assets) and how that property was funded (liabilities = capital raised from others, net assets = the company own capital), setting the two sides side by side; the relationship assets = liabilities + net assets always holds. The two features the question states, ‘presenting a comparison of assets, liabilities, and net assets as of the closing date’ and ‘showing the financial position’, are exactly the definition of a balance sheet. The question further asks about the consolidated financial statement a parent company prepares by treating the corporate group including its subsidiaries as a single entity, so the consolidated version — the consolidated balance sheet — is the answer. In short, the balance sheet shows financial position (a stock, the balances at one point in time) while the income statement shows operating results (a flow, the changes over one period); once you have that contrast in mind you can answer immediately.

fields.before: The correct answer is エ. A colocation service (housing) is a form of service in which users bring servers and communication equipment that they themselves have purchased and own into a data center operated by a provider and are allowed to install them there. What the provider supplies is the installation space itself: an earthquake-resistant building and racks, uninterruptible power supplies and on-site generators, dedicated air conditioning, security such as entry and exit control, 24-hour monitoring, and high-speed, redundant lines to the Internet. Purchasing the server hardware, and operating and managing the OS and applications that run on it, remain on the user side. The effect obtained is therefore that the costs of facilities such as a server room, and of high-capacity communication lines, which the company would otherwise have to prepare by itself in order to keep providing services with its own servers, can be reduced by sharing the provider facilities. エ, which states exactly this, is the most appropriate.

fields.before: Tell colocation (housing) and hosting apart by asking who owns the server. In colocation, equipment owned by the user is installed in the provider facility and what is rented is the space, power, air conditioning, security, and lines, so what goes down is facility costs and line costs. In hosting, servers owned by the provider are rented, so server purchase costs and the operational workload for the equipment go down as well.

fields.before: The correct answer is ア. Only a and b are appropriate. First, regarding a, an email virus may use the recipient address book to send itself to acquaintances without the infected person noticing, or it may arrive disguised as a trusted party through spoofing of the sender address. In other words, who the mail came from is no guarantee at all that the attachment is safe, so performing a virus check on the attachment even when the mail is from a person you trust is appropriate. Next, regarding b, non-executable files such as audio or images look safe at first glance, but there is a technique of faking the file extension so that the file is in fact an executable, and there are also cases where malicious data that exploits a vulnerability in the application opening the file is embedded in an image or document data file itself, so that a malicious program starts running the moment the file is opened. Therefore performing a virus check regardless of the type of file is appropriate. On the other hand, c is clearly wrong: the preview function automatically interprets and displays the body of a message without any action to open it, so a script or a malicious tag embedded in an HTML mail, or external content that is loaded automatically, can run and infect the machine merely from previewing. Far from being a way to confirm safety, it can itself become the trigger for an infection, so the correct handling of a suspicious email is to delete it without opening it, preview included. Hence only a and b are appropriate, and ア, which lists exactly those and nothing else, is the correct answer.

fields.before: Blank b must be an action that strengthens blank a, so you pick the combination in which a and b hold a valid cause-and-effect relationship. When Company A acquires additional shares (b), the ratio of Company B shares it holds rises, and its voting rights at the shareholders meeting increase. A higher voting-rights ratio strengthens its influence over the appointment and dismissal of directors and over resolutions on important matters, so its managerial control (a) over Company B is strengthened. Holding more than 50% of the voting rights makes effective control possible, and this relationship is called a parent-subsidiary relationship. When the voting rights are roughly 20% or more but 50% or less, control is not reached; the relationship is regarded as one that can exert significant influence, and such a company is called an affiliated company, distinguished from a subsidiary. Therefore イ, with a = managerial control and b = acquiring additional shares, is the correct answer.

fields.before: The correct answer is ウ, VPN (Virtual Private Network). A VPN is a technology that creates a communication path over a public line shared by an unspecified number of users, such as the Internet or a carrier network, by combining authentication, encryption, and tunneling (a mechanism that wraps communication data in another protocol to carry it), so that from the users point of view it looks like a closed line reserved just for them. Laying a physical leased line is expensive, but a VPN can reuse the existing public line while holding down the risk of eavesdropping and tampering, safely connecting sites to each other or connecting remote-work devices to the company LAN. This is exactly the description given in the question, “making a public line usable as if it were a dedicated line”.

fields.before: The correct answer is “ウ Time of day”. An interval scale is one in which, beyond the magnitude and order of values, the intervals (differences) between graduations are equal and meaningful, but the origin (zero) is set merely for convenience, so ratios are not meaningful. For time of day, the interval of one hour is equal everywhere, and the difference between 3 oclock and 5 oclock (2 hours) carries the same meaning as the difference between 10 oclock and 12 oclock. On the other hand, 0 oclock is not an absolute zero but only a conventional reference point, so a ratio calculation such as “6 oclock is twice 3 oclock” is meaningless. The property that differences are meaningful while ratios are not is exactly what fits the definition of an interval scale, so ウ is correct.

fields.before: The correct answer is ア. The Companies Act does not require every stock company to have the same organs; it changes the organs that must be put in place according to the size of the company, and the leading example is the accounting auditor. The Act defines a stock company with stated capital of 500 million yen or more, or total liabilities of 20 billion yen or more, as a large company (Companies Act, Article 2, item 6), and provides that a large company must appoint an accounting auditor (Companies Act, Article 328). The larger a company is, the more stakeholders it has — shareholders, business partners, financial institutions and so on — and the wider the impact of whether the figures in its financial statements can be trusted, so the law compels an accounting check by an outside expert. Only a certified public accountant or an audit corporation may serve as an accounting auditor (Companies Act, Article 337, paragraph 1), and the appointment is made by a resolution of the shareholders meeting (Companies Act, Article 329, paragraph 1). The duties are to audit the financial statements such as the balance sheet and the profit and loss statement together with their supplementary schedules, and to prepare an accounting audit report (Companies Act, Article 396, paragraph 1). The accounting auditor is the only one that satisfies both the criterion of “the size of the company” and the condition of “establishment made mandatory by the Companies Act,” so the answer is ア.

fields.before: The correct answer is ウ. Corporate governance means a mechanism for governing management so that management aligned with the company's objectives is carried out. In a joint-stock company, the shareholders who put up the capital are separated from the executives who actually run the company, so there is a risk that the executives may act against the interests of the shareholders and other stakeholders (customers, employees, business partners, local communities, and so on), or commit fraud, or go out of control. Corporate governance therefore puts in place bodies such as the shareholders meeting, the board of directors, outside directors, auditors (the board of auditors), and the accounting auditor, in order to monitor and check management and to ensure transparency of management and accountability. In other words, it is about the structure and mechanism of who checks the executives and secures sound management, and the statement in choice ウ corresponds exactly to that.

fields.before: Incorrect. Email has neither encryption nor tamper detection as a standard feature, so an attacker who controls a server it passes through or the communication path can rewrite the body or swap out an attachment (for example replacing the attachment with malware, or altering a bank account number for a transfer). In other words, integrity is not guaranteed. To confirm that the contents have not been altered in transit, you need a mechanism such as S/MIME or PGP, in which the sender attaches an electronic signature and the recipient verifies the signature and the hash value. An electronic signature achieves both tamper detection and confirmation of the sender identity at the same time, which is the flip side of the fact that the premise of this option does not hold.

fields.before: The correct answer is イ, consistency with the needs of the system client (the party placing the order). System requirements definition is the most upstream process in the system development life cycle. In it, you draw out what stakeholders such as the client and the user departments want to achieve in their business, organize that into the functions, performance, and constraints the system must have, and finally reach agreement with the client. The requirements produced here become the starting point for all of the later design, programming, and testing, so the only yardstick that can measure whether the requirements themselves are good is not the deliverables of later processes but the needs of the client, which are the source of those requirements. If work moves ahead with requirements that conflict with what the client truly needs, then even if the design, the program, and the tests are all built correctly from a technical standpoint, the finished system cannot be used in the actual business, which is the worst kind of rework. In addition, an error in the requirements becomes more expensive to fix the further downstream it travels, so it is important to compare the content with the client during requirements definition, confirm that nothing is missing and that there is no difference in interpretation, and reach agreement. Therefore the appropriate criterion for evaluating system requirements is consistency with the client needs, and イ is correct.

fields.before: Whether the design method is appropriate is an evaluation viewpoint of the system design process, which decides how the requirements are to be realized. What requirements definition decides is what is to be realized; it is not the stage that specifies the method of realization. Moreover, no matter how excellent the design method may be, it is meaningless if the original requirements conflict with the client needs, so it is not appropriate as a criterion for evaluating the requirements themselves.

fields.before: OEM stands for Original Equipment Manufacturer (manufacturing under another company brand), which refers to producing products sold under another company brand name. It denotes a form of contract manufacturing, not a production method for reducing inventory, so it is incorrect.
fields.after: OEM stands for Original Equipment Manufacturer (manufacturing under another company’s brand), which refers to producing products sold under another company’s brand name. It denotes a form of contract manufacturing, not a production method for reducing inventory, so it is incorrect.

fields.before: Be careful not to confuse it with BPO, CIM, and OEM: BPO is the outsourcing of business operations, CIM is the computer-based integration of production information, and OEM is contract manufacturing under another company brand. None of them is a production method for reducing inventory.
